subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering — Finnegans
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@finnegans.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering — Finnegans

Anna — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call (TL;DR at the top, details below):

TL;DR: Finnegans is experiencing noisy-tenant effects on shared endpoints which are impacting p99 latency and causing cost overages for a subset of customers. Primary asks: per-customer rate limits & quotas, policy-based per-customer routing (hot/warm/cold tiering), and visibility for billing/chargeback. Next steps: tech deep-dive with Marissa next week + a scoped pilot for 3 months.

What we heard (pain points)
- Noisy neighbors: Some customers spike traffic and degrade latency for others; impacts SLA commitments to your customers.
- Lack of per-tenant throttles/quotas: Current system has coarse limits at service-level only; cannot protect high-value customers or enforce fair share.
- Billing/chargeback friction: Limited token-level visibility per customer makes it hard to reconcile overages and attribute costs.

Current stack you described
- Inference: self-hosted on AWS (mixed c5/g4 instances) with an autoscaling front-end on ECS; single shared model endpoints per region.
- Orchestration: custom Lambda-based routing + API Gateway.
- Observability: Datadog traces + internal usage logging; logs are post-processed and often delayed.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
1) Per-customer rate limiting and quotas that can be configured per plan and enforced with millisecond accuracy (p99 latency preserved for tiered customers).
2) Per-customer routing/policies: ability to pin VIP customers to dedicated pools or apply soft tiering (hot/warm) automatically.
3) Token-level billing exports and attribution so finance can do chargeback and reconcile invoices.
4) SLA: visible SLOs and alerts for noisy tenant events with automated mitigations.

Potential Redwood approaches we discussed
- Per-tenant quotas & rate limits enforced at the gateway + token accounting for billing exports.
- Policy rules for routing: route by customer label to dedicated pools (Reserved) or shared pools with quotas and fallback.
- Tiering: implement hot/warm lanes with automatic promotion based on activity and priority.
- Visibility: token-level logs exported to your billing pipeline and Datadog integration for real-time dashboards.

Open questions (from our side)
- Do you have any customers that require complete physical isolation (on-prem or VPC) vs logical isolation?
- What is your current monthly token volume per customer (approx) and 95/99th percentile traffic delta between customers?

Next steps
1) Marissa (cc'd) to run a technical deep-dive next Wednesday (2026-02-11) to map routing hooks and auth flow.
2) We'll draft a 3-month pilot scope (MAP) and an initial config for quotas/routing for 10 customers. Attached initial MAP and a short one-pager on rate-limit approaches.
3) Finnegans to share sample billing exports and a short top-10 customer traffic profile.

Attachments: Finnegans-MAP-v1.xlsx (draft MAP), rate-limits-overview.pdf (concept doc)

Thanks again — I’ll coordinate calendars for the deep-dive.
—
Ben Carter

From: Anna Li <anna.li@finnegans.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@finnegans.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering — Finnegans

Ben — great write-up, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Isolation: we do have two strategic customers that require physical separation (they are in healthcare), so VPC/on-prem options are a must for those two. For the rest, logical isolation + quotas would be fine.
- Volumes: average monthly tokens/customer for top 10 is ~12M, but the top 3 can spike to 8–10x baseline during end-of-quarter processing. That's where the noisy neighbor issue is most acute.
- Billing: we can provide a sample billing export (CSV) — will send that to Marissa by Monday.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) If we pin a customer to a dedicated pool, what is the minimum capacity commit? (roughly how many concurrent requests / tokens per second)
2) For tiering, can we do soft promotion where a tenant moves from warm -> hot automatically for short spikes? We want promotions to be fast but not cause churn across pools.

We’re available for the deep-dive on 2026-02-11 at 11:00 PT. Looking forward to Marissa’s notes.

—
Anna Li
Head of Platform Engineering | Finnegans Financial
anna.li@finnegans.com | +1 (415) 555-2210

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna.li@finnegans.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering — Finnegans

Adding a few technical notes ahead of our deep-dive (see attached draft MAP for scope):

- Dedicated pool sizing: for a hot-dedicated pool we recommend a minimum commit equivalent to ~150 concurrent tokens/s or a GPU-backed pool sized for your 95th percentile workload. We’ll validate with your sample traces.
- Soft promotion: yes — Redwood supports automated policy-based promotion with hysteresis (e.g., 3 consecutive high-util windows of 30s) to avoid flapping. Promotion can be configured per-plan.
- Quotas & rate limits: enforced at the routing layer (pre-inference) so noisy tenants are throttled before consuming GPU cycles; we also keep token-exact metering for billing exports.
- Fallbacks: customers routed to warm lanes can automatically fall back to shared pools with a degraded p99 SLO; policies can prefer retry/backoff rules for end-user requests.

Action items for the deep-dive:
- Anna/Tom: share one week of request traces (sample) + billing CSV before EOD Monday.
- Ben: I’ll bring a recommended initial config for 10 customers (quotas + promotion thresholds) and a sizing guide for dedicated pools.
- Finnegans: confirm whether the two healthcare customers require HSM/KMS integration for keys (if so we’ll include Private deployment options).

See you Wednesday at 11:00 PT.
—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0188
